claims.statement: Tom Allen shot Timothy Confoy in the Champions' Rest, his retired pugilists' drinking resort on Market Street, early on Thursday 1899-02-23.
claims.excerpt: was shot y Allen in the retired pugilists’

claims.statement: Timothy Confoy died late on Sunday night on the operating table at City Hospital after being shot by Tom Allen.
claims.excerpt: Confoy died late Sunday night on the operating table in the City Hospital.

claims.statement: Confoy said before he died that he had caused no difficulty in Allen's place and knew of no reason Allen should have fired on him.
claims.excerpt: he knew of no reason why Allen should have fired upon him.

claims.statement: Allen says he fired after seeing Confoy make a movement as if to draw a pistol.
claims.excerpt: saw Confoy make a movement as if to draw

claims.statement: Allen says Confoy had trouble with him some weeks before and came into the saloon seeking to renew it.

claims.statement: A revolver was found on the floor near where Confoy fell; it had not yet been identified as Confoy's.
claims.excerpt: A revolver was found on the floor near the pot where Confoy fell.

claims.statement: Tom Allen was held as a prisoner in the Four Courts holdover.
claims.excerpt: Allen, who is a prisoner in the Four Courts holdover, passed Sunday afternoon

claims.statement: Tom Allen refused to see his friends, who called at the holdover on Sunday afternoon.
claims.excerpt: he refused himself from an interview with any of them

claims.statement: Told on Sunday night that Confoy was dead, Tom Allen expressed mild regret that the shots proved fatal.
claims.excerpt: he expressed mild regret that the shots proved fatal and then went to sleep.

claims.statement: A coroner's inquest into Confoy's death was set for 10 o'clock on Tuesday morning.
claims.excerpt: The Coroner's inquest on the death of Confoy will be held at 10 o'clock Tuesday morning.

claims.statement: Tom Allen was born in Birmingham, England, in 1810, as printed.
claims.excerpt:
Tom Allen was born in Birmingham, Eng-
land, in 1810.

claims.statement: Tom Allen began his pugilistic career in England in 1861.
claims.excerpt: Allen began his pugilistic career in the old country in 1861.

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought a draw with Joe Ge (name cut off in the scan) in March 1867.
claims.excerpt: fought several stiff battles, including a draw with Joe Ge in March, 1867.

claims.statement: Tom Allen was chosen to second Tommy Kelly of Baltimore against Billy Parkinson of Pottsville, Pa., at Acquia Creek, Vermont, in 1867.
claims.excerpt: Allen had been selected to second Témmy Kelly of Baltimore in a finish fight with Billy Parkinson of Pottsville, Pa.

claims.statement: Tom Allen pulled a navy pistol and announced he would kill referee William E. Harding if Kelly did not get the decision.
claims.excerpt: announced that he would kiil Harding !f Kelly ddn’t get the decision on alleged fouls.

claims.statement: Tom Allen cut the ropes and carried Kelly out of the ring.
claims.excerpt: cut the ropes and carried Kelly out of the ring.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Bill Davis in 43 rounds on Chouteau Island, near St. Louis, on January 12, 1869, his first fight in America.
claims.excerpt: The fight was pulled off on Chouteau Island, near St. Louis, Jan, 12, 1869. Allen wonin 43 rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen lost to Charley Gallagher of Cleveland on Carroll Island, near St. Louis, on February 24, 1869, after about three minutes.
claims.excerpt: on Charle Gallagher of Cleveland, the fight taking place on Carroll Island

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Mike McCoole on Foster's Island on July 15, 1869, for a purse and the excursion money; a riot followed.
claims.excerpt: Mike McCoole of St. Louis and Allen fought on Foster's Island, July 15, for a

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Charley Gallagher again on Foster's Island on August 17, 1869; Gallagher was declared the winner.
claims.excerpt: Allen afterwards took on Charley Gallagher a second time, defeating him on Foster’s Island, Aug. 17, 1869.

claims.statement: Tom Allen lost to Jem Mace in ten rounds at Kinnerville, near New Orleans, on May 10, 1870, for a $5000 prize.
claims.excerpt: Allen's best known fight was with Jem Mace at Kinnerville, near New Orieans, La., May 10, 1870.

claims.statement: Joe Coburn declined to fight Tom Allen, and Mike McCoole was given a second match instead.
claims.excerpt: Joe Coburn declined to fight Allen and Mike McCoole was accommodated with a second contest.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Mike McCoole on Chouteau Island on September 23, 1873, so badly that spectators begged McCoole's seconds to take him out of the ring.
claims.excerpt: They fought on Chouteau Isiand, Sept. 23. 1873. Allen made quick work of McCoole

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Joe Goss in Boone County, Kentucky, in 1876 for the championship of America and $2000; Goss was declared winner on a foul after 21 rounds.
claims.excerpt: The fight took place in Boone County, Ky., in 1876. After 21 rounds Goss was declared winner on a foul.

claims.statement: After the Goss fight, Tom Allen was arrested and jailed in Kentucky on a charge of prize fighting.
claims.excerpt: After the fight Allen was arrested and jailed in that State on a charge of prize fighting.

claims.statement: Allen was released on bond, jumped it, and went to England.
claims.excerpt: He was released on bond, jumped his bond and went to England.

claims.statement: Tom Allen spent about a year in England on the race tracks, then returned to America.
claims.excerpt: After a year on the other side, which he put in on the race tracks, he returned to this country

claims.statement: Tom Allen challenged John L. Sullivan to a fight in New York; the challenge came to nothing.
claims.excerpt: by offering to fight John L. Sullivan, After issuing that challenge, which never bore fruit

claims.statement: Tom Allen returned to St. Louis and opened a saloon on Market Street.
claims.excerpt: Allen returned to St. Lou's and opened his saloon on Market st.

claims.statement: Soon after returning to St. Louis, Allen's Kentucky bondsmen came with requisition papers for his arrest as a fugitive.
claims.excerpt: appeared here with requisition papers for his arrest as a fugative from justice.

claims.statement: Allen was freed by a writ of habeas corpus argued before Judge Claiborne in the Court of Criminal Correction, and his Kentucky bondsmen went home without him.
claims.excerpt: Allen’s lawyers secured his release by writ of habeas corpus which was argued before Judge Claiborne in the Court of Criminal Correction.

claims.statement: Tom Allen's last boxing appearance was four friendly rounds with Tom Kelly at Union Baseball Park on July 4, 1884.
claims.excerpt: was on July 4, 1884, at Union Baseball Park when he and Tom Kelly boxed four friendly rounds.

notes: Article 180 is a 1899 life summary, so most claims are retrospective. Shooting date conflict: this article says 'early Thursday morning' (taken as 1899-02-23, medium confidence), while article 179 (dated 1899-02-26) says the shooting was early that Sunday. Birth year is printed 1810; the brief gives 1839-1903, so the birth claim is low confidence. Kelly/Parkinson place printed as 'Acquia Creek, Vermont'. Several OCR errors ('Allea', 'Isiand', 'wonin', 'fugative', 'Témmy').
